messages:
jamie: FYI high-priority ticket from Acme. Go SDK consumers get: \"module declares its path \"github.com/acme/sdk\" at revision v1.4.0\" after we published v1.4.0 tag. Customer says they removed a local replace before tagging. Repro steps attached.
kevin: Can you paste the exact error and their go.mod? usually this is import path vs tag mismatch.
jamie: Error from `go get`: 
```
go: github.com/acme/sdk@v1.4.0: reading github.com/acme/sdk/go.mod: unexpected module path \"github.com/acme/sdk/v1\"
```
Customer go.mod: 
```
module github.com/acme/sdk

go 1.20

require (
    github.com/our/dep v0.3.0
)
```
They say their repo previously had a `replace` to `../sdk-fork` during dev and CI removed it before tagging. They pushed tag v1.4.0 and their private proxy (internal goproxy) returned 200 for zip but go mod read fails.
eli: That error suggests the module's go.mod declares `/v1` while tag is v1.x — go expects major versions >v1 not encoded in path unless v2+. But error shows unexpected module path \"github.com/acme/sdk/v1\" which means the taged module has a go.mod with module line including /v1. Any chance their release process rewrote go.mod?
jamie: Customer attached `git ls-tree` for the tag and `git show v1.4.0:go.mod` output:
```
module github.com/acme/sdk/v1

// accidental change from release script
```
They claim they never edited go.mod manually for v1.4.0.
kevin: Two plausible causes: 1) The tag points to a commit from the fork that used a v1 path, 2) their release CI did a module path rewrite (we've seen scripts that 'bump module path' for internal builds). Ask them to run `git rev-list -n 1 v1.4.0` and `git show <sha>:go.mod` and compare with main HEAD.
jamie: They ran `git rev-list -n 1 v1.4.0` -> `abc123` and `git show abc123:go.mod` shows `/v1`. But HEAD at main has `module github.com/acme/sdk` (no /v1). So tag points to a commit where go.mod was wrong. Customer says they did a force-push of the tag after rolling back but Go proxy cached the earlier tag zip and SumDB mismatch occurs.
eli: If their internal GOPROXY cached the earlier artifact, consumers will see the cached zip with the wrong go.mod. Workarounds: purge the proxy cache for that module+version, or create a new v1.4.1 release that points to the corrected commit. Also `go clean -modcache` won't help consumers hitting proxy.
kevin: For immediate relief advise them to: 1) delete tag v1.4.0 on the remote and the proxy cache, 2) re-create v1.4.0 at the correct commit (not ideal), or 3) publish v1.4.1 with proper go.mod. Note: force-updating tags is bad with proxies.
jamie: Customer asks about why `replace` earlier matter. They had `replace github.com/acme/sdk => ../sdk-fork` and local builds worked, but when tagging CI removed replace, different commit got tagged.
eli: That fits — if you have a replace and then CI builds from a different checkout or merges autopatches, the tag could be made from the forked tree or a temporary branch. We should recommend adding a release checklist: ensure go.mod module path matches intended upstream before tagging, `git show` the tag commit.
ops-bot: Ticket #T-3921 created and escalated to eng-release for guidance. :rotating_light:
kevin: Also share steps for them to verify on their side:
```
# verify tag commit
git fetch --tags origin
sha=$(git rev-list -n 1 v1.4.0)
git show $sha:go.mod

# check proxy artifact
curl -I \"$GOPROXY/github.com/acme/sdk/@v/v1.4.0.zip\"
```
If `go.mod` inside zip declares `/v1` then proxy is serving wrong content.
jamie: Customer tried `curl` and saw the zip from proxy differs from repo. They will purge proxy cache and either re-tag or bump to v1.4.1.
eli: Suggestion for us: we should add a docs blurb about never force-pushing tags when using proxies and how to check module path vs semver. I'll draft one.
kevin: Marking as ack, awaiting customer follow-up. :thumbsup:
